# Node fixtures of smtpwire

These scripts record what the real nodemailer (the one in
`web-nodejs/node_modules`) does on the wire. The Go tests replay the
recordings. They are fixtures: once the Node console is gone, the recordings
stay as the specification and the scripts can be deleted.

No mail leaves a recording. Every script talks to a server it starts itself
on 127.0.0.1 (`sink.js`).

## Running

In the dev image, from the repository root:

    betterdesk-server/console/mail/smtpwire/testdata/nodeoracle/run.sh            # all three
    betterdesk-server/console/mail/smtpwire/testdata/nodeoracle/run.sh sessions   # one of sessions, vectors, e2e

`run.sh` sets `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to `../certs/trusted.pem`, because the
transport is created exactly as `services/emailService.js` creates it and so
has no option for extra root certificates. The certificates under `../certs`
were made once by `../gencerts` (`go run ./console/mail/smtpwire/testdata/gencerts
console/mail/smtpwire/testdata/certs` in `betterdesk-server`); making them
again means recording again.

| Script | Output | Replayed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `record_sessions.js` (tables in `scenarios.js`) | `../sessions.json` | `TestSessions` |
| `record_vectors.js` | `../vectors.json` | the `Test...Vectors` tests |
| `record_e2e.js` | `../e2e_sessions.json` | the integration test of the mail service (package `console/mail`) |

## The sink and its scripts

`sink.js` plays the server side of one connection from a script and records
the client's side. `sink_test.go` is the same thing in Go. The header of
`sink.js` describes the script format (greeting, rules per command verb, ops)
and the recorded events.

## sessions.json

A list of scenarios, one per line:

- `name`, `call` (`send` or `verify`)
- `hostname`: what `os.hostname()` returned (`{value}`) or that it threw (`{error: true}`)
- `options`: `host`, `port` (the port the sink listened on, 0 for nodemailer's
  default), `secure`, `user`, `pass`, `tlsVerify` and the timeouts in ms
- `envelope`: the envelope `smtp-connection` was given (after mime-node, or
  the one a scenario forced in), `message`: `{s}` bytes as Latin-1 characters
  or `{gen: {seed, size, alphabet}}` for generated bytes
- `dns`: the A (`a`) and AAAA (`aaaa`) records the recorder gave the host of
  the scenario; without it the lookups were those of the machine
- `server`: the sink script, `{listen: false}` when nothing listened
- `client`: the recorded events of the client's side
- `outcome`: `{ok: true}`, `{info: {...}}` or `{error: {message, code, response, responseCode, command, ...}}`
- `cmp`: what a replay does not compare, with the reason in `scenarios.js`
  and in the comment of `TestSessions`

## e2e_sessions.json

Made by calling `sendEmail`, `sendAlertEmail`, `sendHelpRequestEmail` and
`testConnection` of the real `services/emailService.js`. Its database
adapter is replaced by a stub whose `getSetting('smtp_config')` returns the
session's setting; everything else is the real code, with the environment in
`env` (no `SMTP_*`, `PANEL_PUBLIC_URL` or `PUBLIC_URL` variables).

Top level: `nodemailer` (version), `env`, `panelBaseUrl` (what
`getPanelBaseUrl()` returned), `sessions`. Each session:

- `name`
- `hostname`: the machine name during the call (`console.example.test`)
- `config`: the value `getSetting('smtp_config')` returned: a JSON string, an
  object for the sessions stored as object, `null` for no setting. Its `port`
  is `port`, the port the sink listened on (a closed port when `server` is
  `null`); a replay has to put its own port there.
- `call`: `{fn, args}`, the function and its arguments
- `result`: what the function returned (`true`, `false`, `{success}` or
  `{success, error}`). An error text can hold the port as a number
  (`connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:45109`).
- `logs`: the console lines of the call, `{level, text}`, with the port
  replaced by `{port}`
- `server`: the sink script (`null`: nothing listened)
- `client`: the client's side of the session as the sink recorded it:
  `{e: "line", s}` for every command line (bytes as Latin-1 characters),
  `{e: "tls", sni}` where TLS started, `{e: "data", b64}` for the bytes after
  DATA up to and including the end line (base64, always in full here),
  `{e: "eof"}` when the client closed. No events: the call made no connection.

The DATA bytes hold what nodemailer generated for that call: a Message-ID, a
Date and MIME boundaries that differ on every run.
